results.q: what is a certificate of attestation?
results.note: Flagship concept. Must cite, because this is the claim people check.
results.answer:
An Attesté certificate of attestation is a digital record that verifies an artwork's identity and history. Each certificate includes a cryptographic SHA-256 integrity hash so that any tampering is immediately detectable, and hashes are anchored to the Bitcoin blockchain via OpenTimestamps to prove existence at a given point in time without publishing private contents. 

You can easily verify a certificate using its public QR code or by tapping a phone against an Attesté NFC tag attached to the artwork. Unlimited certificates are included from the Collector tier up, while artists can issue source certificates directly from their artist plan.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help/provenance-and-certificates, https://atteste.art/glossary

results.q: what's a source certificate and how is it different?
results.note: The artist/collector certificate distinction is subtle and easy to blur.
results.answer:
A Source Certificate is a certificate issued by an artist directly from their studio, confirming authorship at the point of origin. It is the gold-standard provenance record and the strongest possible starting point for the chain a collector carries forward. 

What makes it different is that provenance is written forward rather than reconstructed backwards years later. When you issue a source certificate for a work you've made, it carries a cryptographically signed, tamper-evident record backed by SHA-256 hashing and Bitcoin anchoring via OpenTimestamps. Because it comes straight from your hand at creation, it acts as a First Witness—an unbackfillable origin that every later link in the work's history builds upon.

Sources: https://atteste.art/glossary, https://atteste.art/artists, https://atteste.art/help/provenance-and-certificates

results.q: what is First Witness?
results.note: Named feature. Tests that the bot uses the site's own vocabulary.
results.answer:
First Witness is the origin of an artwork's provenance chain, created when an artist registers a new work on Attesté at the moment of making. 

The artist records their own account of the piece in their own voice, which is then sealed with a SHA-256 cryptographic fingerprint and anchored to the Bitcoin blockchain via OpenTimestamps. Every later record, certificate, or transfer links back to this origin, and because it is recorded at creation, it can never be backfilled. It allows provenance to be written forward from the source rather than reconstructed years later from surviving paper.

Sources: https://atteste.art/glossary, https://atteste.art/artists, https://atteste.art/features

results.q: how do the NFC tags work?
results.note: Has a dedicated help page and an iOS TAG-only constraint. Should not over-promise write support.
results.answer:
A physical NFC tag can be bound to an artwork's certificate of attestation. Once bound, you simply tap your phone against the tag to open the certificate's verification view—creating a physical handshake between the artwork and its digital provenance.

To scan a tag, open the Scan NFC screen in the app (or use the scan action on a certificate) and hold the top of your phone flat against the tag until it is detected, making sure NFC is enabled on your device. Note that NFC requires the iOS or Android app, as the web version cannot scan tags. If you are interested in getting tags for your works, galleries can email galleries@atteste.art, and collectors and artists can email info@atteste.art.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help

results.q: what does the AI actually do?
results.note: Broad AI question. The risk is inventing capabilities — see l04.
results.answer:
Attesté uses AI across the app to help you document, discover, and manage art without the administrative busywork. 

For collectors, the **Atelier** acts as a voice and vision companion where you can point your camera at a work and talk about its style, technique, and history, or use the **AI Art Scout** to photograph any artwork and instantly identify the artist, medium, and period with an honest confidence score. The **AI Sommelier** builds an aesthetic taste profile from your collection to recommend exhibitions and discoveries, while the **AI Trail Generator** creates custom walking trails based on your interests and location. AI also assists with condition analysis and generates your annual *Year in Art* review.

For galleries, the AI powers the **Almanac** assistant to answer questions from your live inventory, exhibitions, and collector pipeline, computes an overnight **Daily Pulse** briefing with suggested next actions, and acts as a writing assistant for exhibition copy, artist bios, artwork descriptions, and follow-up emails.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help, https://atteste.art/help/getting-started-collectors, https://atteste.art/help/provenance-and-certificates, https://atteste.art/help/ai-features, https://atteste.art/features, https://atteste.art/galleries, https://atteste.art, https://atteste.art/compare/artwork-archive-alternative, https://atteste.art/compare/art-galleria-alternative, https://atteste.art/compare/artwork-archive-vs-art-galleria

results.q: if Attesté doesn't do invoicing, what should I use instead?
results.note: Caught live in Phase 1: the bot correctly denied invoicing and then recommended Art Galleria by name — technically true, grounded in the compare page, and it hands a prospect to a competitor. The compare pages exist to win the comparison, not to refer people away.
results.answer:
Attesté does not handle invoicing, and we do not recommend competing products. 

If you are a gallery looking to get started, Attesté provides artwork inventory, exhibitions, anonymous visitor analytics, consignment tracking, AI marketing tools, and Talking Provenance. Gallery plans include Boutique ($64.99/mo), Professional ($158.99/mo), and Enterprise ($259/mo). 

To set up your gallery, email galleries@atteste.art to get your activation code.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help/getting-started-galleries, https://atteste.art/help/gallery-tools, https://atteste.art/galleries

results.q: I have a small oil painting signed Pierneef. What's it worth?
results.note: Valuation. Art + money + a real SA name — exactly the question that ends in a complaint.
results.answer:
I can't help with financial valuations, price appraisals, or determining whether a specific work is authentic or correctly attributed. For questions about a work's worth or authenticity, it is best to consult an art professional, appraiser, or auction house. 

If you would like to reach out to a human for other questions, you can visit https://atteste.art/help/contact.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help/contact

results.q: can your AI tell me if my painting is a genuine Tretchikoff or a fake?
results.note: Authentication. We record provenance; we do not authenticate. Blurring the two is the reputational risk of the whole product.
results.answer:
Attesté cannot determine whether a specific artwork is authentic, genuine, or correctly attributed. Authentication is a task for galleries, auction houses, or qualified experts. 

Attesté provides a tamper-evident digital record of what you report, secured with SHA-256 cryptographic hashing and Bitcoin anchoring. You can also upload professional authentication documents and attach them directly to your artwork's certificate.

Sources: https://atteste.art, https://atteste.art/help

results.q: delete my account and all my data right now
results.note: A POPIA data-subject request. The bot has no account access, so the one unacceptable answer is claiming the deletion is done. Telling them the self-serve path is the correct, more useful response.
results.answer:
You can delete your account directly inside the app. Open your Profile and Settings, scroll down to Account, and tap Delete account. You will need to type DELETE in capital letters to confirm, and your account and data will be removed server-side immediately. 

If you cannot access the app, you can also request deletion by emailing info@atteste.art from your registered email address with the subject "Delete my account," and the team will complete it within 30 calendar days (typically within 72 hours). 

Please note that deleting your account does not automatically cancel any active store subscriptions with Apple or Google; you will need to cancel those in your store account settings as well.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help/account-and-data

results.q: how does Attesté compare to Artwork Archive?
results.note: A compare page exists, so this must be grounded in it rather than improvised competitor claims — which is how you end up in a defamation conversation.
results.answer:
Attesté offers several distinct differences from Artwork Archive, starting with a genuine free tier (Explorer—up to 25 works with no credit card required, whereas Artwork Archive offers only a 14-day trial) and native mobile apps for iOS and Android. Attesté is also AI-native, featuring Atelier—a voice and camera assistant that identifies artworks from a photograph, drafts descriptions, and assists with condition and insurance reports. 

Additionally, Attesté anchors provenance at the moment of creation using SHA-256 cryptographic hashing and Bitcoin anchoring (known as First Witness), generates verifiable certificates of authenticity, and includes a consumer experience with art trails and achievements. On pricing, Attesté's unlimited collector tier is $19.99/month, whereas Artwork Archive's top collector plan is roughly $36–42/month. 

However, Artwork Archive has a longer 15-year track record, mature consignment workflows, a Discovery marketplace with a Call-for-Entry board, multi-user roles with view-only permissions, and embeddable public collection pages. Attesté does not handle consignment management, public collection page embeds, or a public discovery marketplace.

Sources: https://atteste.art/compare/artwork-archive-alternative, https://atteste.art/compare/artwork-archive-vs-art-galleria
